page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance features dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz, providing 32 physical cores and 64 virtual CPUs across two threads per core. Memory capacity is substantial at 512.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 16 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates without bundled local storage, and includes no dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark testing indicates robust parallel computational capabilities and high cache throughput. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieved a strong multi-core score of 86,393.0 alongside high PassMark CPU results of 58,937.08, supported by strong cryptographic and extended instruction execution. The memory subsystem demonstrated high performance under cached conditions, reaching 4,144.0 GB/sec on small-block read tests and a top-quartile PassMark memory score of 2,866.53. However, large-block uncached memory operations balanced out to median ranges with 76.39 GB/sec read and 35.1 GB/sec write throughput.

The instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for organizations requiring high RAM density without investing in specialized GPU infrastructure. Because it lacks onboard NVMe storage, persistent data architectures require external network-attached volumes, introducing potential I/O latency dependencies. Performance profiles make Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.16xlarge well adapted for large in-memory data processing, distributed caching layers such as Redis, enterprise database hosting, multi-threaded code compilation, and memory-intensive enterprise application serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by dedicated 2.55 GHz AMD EPYC 7T83 processors on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs, it pairs extensive compute capacity with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. The server includes 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and excludes GPU accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks show top-tier multi-threaded processing, robust encryption speeds, and high cached memory throughput, while large uncached memory transfers and static web serving register in average percentiles. With high memory density per compute core, ecs.r7a.16xlarge is engineered for memory-heavy enterprise deployments, including large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, multi-threaded software build pipelines, and transactional database workloads that utilize remote storage.
